title: There's a Planet Where It Rains Glass Sideways

scenes.text: There's a planet where it rains glass. Sideways.
It's a giant blue world about sixty-three light years from Earth.
In 2013, the Hubble Space Telescope worked out its color: deep cobalt blue, a lot like Earth seen from space.
But that blue isn't water. It comes from clouds packed with tiny particles of glass.
Daytime temperatures reach nearly two thousand degrees Fahrenheit, and winds blow at more than four thousand miles an hour.
Scientists think the heat melts those particles into droplets, so when it rains, it rains molten glass, blown sideways by the wind.
A full year there lasts just over two days. Still want to visit another planet?

description:
About 63 light years away, there's a deep blue planet where scientists think it rains molten glass, blown sideways by winds of over 4,000 miles an hour.
Hubble found its cobalt color in 2013. The blue comes from glass particles in its clouds, not oceans.
It circles its star in just over two days.
Which exoplanet should we cover next?
